anTV

A single-file “10-foot” media launcher for a PC connected to a TV. Pick a card with a remote, game pad or phone, and anTV opens the app fullscreen. File name: tvhub.py.

Python 3 + GTK3Linux Mint (Cinnamon/X11)Windows 10/11 via MSYS2 Launcher is ad-freev0.25.1App pop-upsTested: Windows 11 & Linux Mint
About the screenshots The desktop screens (home, menus, settings) were drawn from the app’s own source: its colors, fonts, sizes, rows and labels. They are marked Illustration. The GTK app itself could not be started in the environment used to write this guide. The phone remote screens are marked Real render: they are the actual page that anTV serves, rendered in a browser. Your own screen may differ in fonts and spacing.

▌Overview

anTV is meant for a computer plugged into a TV, often with a second monitor. It shows large cards for your streaming sites, local players and Android apps. Everything is operable from a distance: arrow keys, a Fire TV remote, an Xbox controller, or your phone.

Launch anything

Websites in a kiosk browser, local programs, Node.js apps, and Android apps via adb or Waydroid.

Control from the couch

Keyboard, Fire TV remote, Xbox controller, or a PIN-protected phone page with D-pad, touchpad, typing and app buttons.

Pop-ups on top of anything

Reminders and alerts from your apps (Tasks first) appear over a movie or app, and you answer with the controller, phone or mouse.

One-key escape

Ctrl+Alt+K kills whatever app is running and returns to anTV.

Everything is an option

Card size and shape, fonts, background slideshow, clock, idle fade, favorites layout: all in Settings.

▌Features

Main screen

  • Header: “anTV” title, settings cog, a clock (12-hour, 24-hour or off) and a status line.
  • Favorites row: scrolls sideways or wraps as a grid. Starred apps appear here, even if they sit inside folders. You can also add the built-in Web Browser and Local Media cards.
  • All apps grid: everything else. “Show other apps” can be turned off.
  • Folders: hold apps, can be nested, and have their own card or picture. A breadcrumb shows where you are; Back, Esc or a “◂ Back” card goes up one level.
  • Cards: small, medium, large or extra large, in wide (16:9), classic (4:3), square or poster (2:3) shapes. All cards share one size. A card can have a picture (fill or fit) or be “picture only”.
  • Background and idle fade: a background picture or a slideshow folder (interval and shuffle). After a quiet period the cards fade so the picture shows through.
  • Default backgrounds: three ready-made pictures ship with anTV and are used until you choose your own picture or slideshow folder. You can add your own pictures to that folder from Settings.
  • Hide and Quit: H hides anTV to the taskbar; Settings has Hide and Quit buttons too.
  • Utility cards: “+ Add app”, “+ Node.js app” and “+ Install APK”.

Launching apps

TypeWhat happens
WebsiteOpens in a kiosk Chromium or Firefox window, with a separate browser profile per service (so each site keeps its own login).
Program (command)Runs a local command such as kodi or vlc --fullscreen.
Node.js appInstalls, starts the server, waits for its port, opens it in the browser, and stops the server afterwards. Optionally keeps the server running in the background (needed for pop-ups).
Android appLaunches on a Fire TV or other Android device over adb, or on this PC with Waydroid.
FolderOpens a sub-screen of cards.
Web Browser cardA general browser with a picker and its own profile.
Local Media / USBA file browser for your media folders and plugged-in drives, with eject.

Every app runs in its own process group, so closing it cleanly kills the whole tree (browser helpers included).

Input methods

Keyboard

Arrows move, Enter opens, plus single-key shortcuts. See Keyboard shortcuts.

Fire TV remote

Pairs as a Bluetooth keyboard. Buttons are mapped by action (select, back, menu, play/pause, home) and can be re-learned.

Xbox controller

Wired or Bluetooth. Linux reads /dev/input/js*; Windows uses XInput. While Android is open, input is forwarded to it.

Phone remote

Opt-in web page on your Wi-Fi, PIN protected, with four tabs: D-pad, Touchpad, Type, Apps.

Android support

  • Install APKs and launch Android apps on a Fire TV or Android device with adb (including by IP address).
  • Or run Android on this PC with Waydroid, shown fullscreen on the TV screen using a nested weston compositor. Software rendering is chosen automatically when an NVIDIA card is detected.
  • “Android check” in Settings reports the graphics card, Waydroid, weston and wmctrl status.
  • Popular apps: YouTube (web, youtube.com/tv), FreeTube (Flatpak, Linux only), a Piped or Invidious site you enter, and a guided SmartTube install into Waydroid.

Settings

Sections: Apps & favorites, Layout, Look, Screen & browser, Remote & devices, Pop-ups, Your data and About. Two versions of the same settings: a classic dark dialog with tabs (Apps, Main screen, Look, System, About), and an optional TV-friendly full-screen version with huge text and no small controls. See Settings for the walk-through.

1Install

The download (TVHub-all-files-0_25_1.zip) unzips to these items. Keep them together in one folder:

FilePurpose
tvhub.pyThe whole application.
Setup-TVHub.batWindows: double-click to start the installer.
Setup-TVHub.ps1Windows: the installer script itself (keep it next to the .bat and tvhub.py).
backgrounds/Three default background pictures.
tasks/The Tasks app (a Node.js to-do list that sends pop-ups to anTV). See Tasks app.
anTV_Popup_Protocol_Spec.mdThe contract for building apps that send pop-ups to anTV.
anTV (tvhub.py) Handoff Specification.mdDeveloper notes.
TestedanTV has been tested on Windows 11 and Linux Mint, and the features then available worked on both. The newer features (pop-ups, backup, default backgrounds) are written here from the 0.25.1 source.

Linux Mint (Cinnamon / X11)

  1. Install the required packages:

    sudo apt install python3-gi gir1.2-gtk-3.0

  2. Install the helpers you need (all optional):

    sudo apt install xdotool wmctrl      # phone typing, other-app keys, window placement
sudo apt install adb                  # install APKs on Fire TV / Android
sudo apt install vlc chromium         # players and the kiosk browser
sudo apt install flatpak              # only for FreeTube
# Waydroid and weston: only if you want Android apps on this PC

  3. Start anTV from the folder that holds tvhub.py:

    python3 tvhub.py

  4. Add it to the Mint menu and set the close-app hotkeys (once):

    python3 tvhub.py --install

    This creates a “TV Hub” menu entry and registers Ctrl+Alt+K and Super+Esc as global shortcuts for tvhub.py --kill.

Linux has no setup script, only the apt commands above. To add a Node.js app with pop-ups from a terminal, close anTV and run python3 tvhub.py --add-node-app NAME FOLDER [URL] (prints added, updated or exists).

Check the version any time with python3 tvhub.py --version (prints anTV 0.25.1).

Windows 10 / 11

  1. Unzip everything into one folder, then double-click Setup-TVHub.bat.

  2. Accept the administrator prompt. The script installs MSYS2 (Python, PyGObject and GTK3 come from there), updates it (the first run can take several minutes), then installs VLC. Microsoft Edge is already part of Windows.

  3. It asks about optional extras: Node.js LTS, Google Chrome, adding the Tasks app, start-on-login, and a firewall rule for the phone remote (and Node.js apps).

  4. It checks that tvhub.py imports, prints an OK / MISSING summary, and creates TVHub.bat plus Desktop and Start Menu shortcuts. Start anTV from the “TV Hub” shortcut. You can re-run the script any time.

Installer switches (add after the file name from a terminal):

SwitchEffect
-CheckOnly report what is installed (including the anTV version, the tasks folder and whether the Tasks card is set up); change nothing.
-YesNever ask questions. Optional items are installed only if their switch is given.
-Node, -ChromeAlso install Node.js LTS or Google Chrome without asking.
-TasksInstall Node.js and add a Tasks card (from the tasks folder) with pop-ups and keep-running turned on. Close anTV first: the script refuses to run this while anTV is open.
-NoVlcSkip VLC.
-AutostartStart anTV when you log in.
-FirewallAllow the phone remote, and node.exe (so a phone can open Tasks), through Windows Firewall on Private networks.
Windows close-app keyCtrl+Alt+K works while anTV is running. No system shortcut is needed.

2First start

  1. Run anTV. It opens fullscreen on your last monitor, usually the TV.

  2. Wrong screen? Press F1 to move it to the next monitor. The choice is saved. You can also pick it in Settings → Screen & browser → “Show anTV on”.

  3. You will see the default cards: Jellyfin, Plex, Emby, Netflix, Hulu, Peacock, Disney+, YouTube, Kodi and VLC, plus Web Browser, Local Media, and the add cards. Jellyfin and Emby point at localhost servers, so they only work if you run those.

  4. Leave anTV with Esc or Q on the home screen.

3Navigate the home screen

  1. Move between cards with the arrow keys, D-pad or controller. The selected card gets a thick white outline.

  2. Open the selected card with Enter / OK / A button (or Play/Pause).

  3. Settings: move to the ⚙ cog next to “anTV” and press OK, or press S, or the remote’s Menu button.

  4. Back: inside a folder, Back, Esc, Backspace or the “◂ Back” card goes up one level. On the home screen, Back does nothing (so a stray press never quits).

▌Add apps

Press A, or select the + Add app card. One menu covers everything you can add:

A website or program

  1. Choose A website or program…. The Add form opens (a normal dialog with dark, large styling).

  2. Pick the type: Website (kiosk browser), Command (local program), Node.js app, Android app or Folder.

  3. Fill in the name and the address (https://…) or the command (vlc --fullscreen). Optionally set a color, a picture, “favorite”, and “picture only”.

  4. Save. The new card appears in the grid.

Popular apps

Ready-made cards. Nothing is downloaded except by the apps themselves. Choosing one that you already have shows “You already have a … card”.

Node.js app

Press N or use the + Node.js app card. Choose the project folder, the start command (default node server.js) and the address (default http://localhost:3000). In the form, tick Show this app’s pop-ups and Keep its server running in the background if the app sends pop-ups. On launch, anTV shows a status splash while it installs and starts the server, opens it in the browser, and stops the server when you close the app. Esc cancels the splash. Requires Node.js.

Remove or edit

Select a card and press Delete to remove it (folders with content ask first). For editing, ordering and moving, use Settings → Apps & favorites.

▌Favorites & folders

  1. Open Settings → Apps & favorites, select an app and choose Toggle favorite ★. Starred apps show in the Favorites row at the top, even when they live inside a folder.

  2. Create a folder: + New folder there, or Add app → A folder to organize apps… on the home screen.

  3. Put an app in a folder: select it in Settings and choose Move to folder…. Folders can nest; a folder cannot be moved into itself.

  4. Choose how favorites are shown in Settings → Layout → Favorites row: Scroll sideways or Grid: show all.

▌Close a running app

While a kiosk app has the screen, anTV’s own keys do not work, so use one of these. Each kills the app’s whole process tree, runs any stop commands, and returns you to anTV.

FromHow
Keyboard (Linux)Ctrl+Alt+K or Super+Esc (set up by --install)
Keyboard (Windows)Ctrl+Alt+K
Terminalpython3 tvhub.py --kill
Xbox controllerThe Xbox (guide) button
Phone remoteThe red Close app / Home button on the D-pad tab
Fire TV remoteHome, once you have taught it in Remote control setup

▌Settings

Open with the ⚙ cog, S, or the remote’s Menu key. Settings are dark with thick text so they stay readable from the couch.

Classic dialog (default)

A tabbed dialog: Apps, Main screen, Look, System, Pop-ups, Your data, About, with Save, Cancel, Hide anTV and Quit anTV. Best with a mouse or keyboard. The About tab shows the version and history, a Keyboard shortcuts button, and a checkbox to switch to the TV-friendly screen.

TV-friendly (10-foot) screen

Turn on “TV-friendly settings (this screen)” under About. Then the cog opens a full-screen list: sections on the left, options on the right, hints along the bottom.

  1. Use ▲▼ to choose a section, then Enter or ▶ to open it.

  2. On an option row, ◀▶ changes its value (or toggles it). Enter opens a picker, menu or sub-screen.

  3. Back returns from the options to the sections.

  4. The section list ends with Hide anTV (minimize) and Quit anTV (Quit asks first); the footer has Quit, Hide, Discard and Save buttons.

  5. Changes stay in memory until you save. Press Menu or Start, choose ✔ Save and close, or press the green Save button. ✖ Discard changes throws them away. Back with unsaved changes asks: Save, Discard or Keep editing.

Add flows save by themselvesPopular apps, Install APK and the Add screens opened from TV settings save immediately, so any unsaved TV-settings changes are saved first.

▌Pop-ups from apps

New in 0.25: an app can announce something (a reminder, a finished job, an alert) and anTV draws a card on top of whatever is on the TV: a fullscreen kiosk browser, a movie in VLC, Waydroid, or anTV’s own home screen. You answer with the controller, the phone remote or the mouse. The card never takes keyboard focus, so a movie keeps its keys while the card is up.

Turn it on for an app

  1. Add the app as a Node.js app (or website). In its form tick Show this app’s pop-ups (reminders, alerts) on top of other apps. For Node.js apps also tick Keep its server running in the background: pop-ups only arrive while the app’s server is running, and this makes anTV start it at launch and leave it running when you close the app.

  2. Open Settings → Pop-ups. Pop-up sources should now read something like “1 of 1 connected”.

  3. Choose Send a test pop-up to see the card.

You can also listen to an app that has no card: in Pop-up sources choose + Add a source (address)… and enter its address, for example http://localhost:3000. Remove a source from the same list.

Answer a pop-up

InputAction
Left / Right (D-pad, controller, phone D-pad)Choose a button
OK / A / EnterRun the chosen button (the first one is selected when the card appears)
Back / B / EscDismiss
Mouse or phone touchpad clickClick a button
Up, Down, Menu, HomeNever taken by pop-ups, so volume and “close app” keep working

The card disappears after its timeout. If a button was Open, anTV closes whatever is running, waits about 3 seconds and launches the app’s card (the card must exist).

Pop-up settings

OptionMeaning
Show pop-ups from my appsMaster on/off (default on).
Where pop-ups appearTop right (default), top left, bottom right or bottom left.
Keep a pop-up up for0–300 s in steps of 5 (default 20; 0 = until dismissed). An app can set its own timeout.
Play a soundOn by default. Low-priority pop-ups are silent.
Pop-up sourcesShows how many sources are connected; add or remove source addresses.
Send a test pop-upShows a sample card.
Let other programs on this PC send pop-upsTurns on the push address (below). Off by default.
…also from other devices on my networkLets other machines on your network use the push address. Off by default.
Show the address and keyDisplays the push address (default port 8767) and the secret key.

Queue and priority

  • One card shows at a time; up to 20 wait in a queue.
  • High priority pop-ups jump the queue and replace a normal one on screen. Low ones are silent.
  • A repeated pop-up (same app and id) is ignored for 5 minutes.
  • If an app goes away, anTV reconnects on its own (retry every 3 to 30 seconds).

Two ways apps send pop-ups

A. Feed (preferred)

anTV connects to the app. The app serves GET /antv.json (name, color, events path) and a Server-Sent-Events stream (default /api/events) that carries event: popup messages. The buttons call the app back (for example “Done”), using web addresses that point at the app itself.

GET /antv.json  →  {"protocol":1,"name":"Tasks","color":"#ffb84d","events":"/api/events"}
event: popup
data: {"id":"task:abc:1","title":"Take out the trash","tag":"Chores · Due 5:00 PM",
       "actions":[{"label":"✓ Done","method":"PATCH","url":"/api/lists/L1/tasks/abc","body":{"done":true}},
                  {"label":"Open","kind":"open"}]}

B. Push

For a script or program that cannot run a server. Turn on Let other programs on this PC send pop-ups, read the address and key with Show the address and key, then:

POST http://127.0.0.1:8767/notify
X-Antv-Token: <key shown in anTV>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "app": "Backup script", "title": "Backup finished", "body": "42 GB copied", "color": "#7ee08a" }

Answers: 200 accepted, 401 wrong key, 400 nothing to show. The body must be under 8 KB, and button addresses must be full http://… URLs.

For app authorsPop-up fields: id, title, body, tag, color (#rrggbb), priority (low/normal/high), timeout, sound, up to 3 actions (label up to 24 characters). anTV always adds a Dismiss button. The full contract is in anTV_Popup_Protocol_Spec.md from the download.
Keep secrets out of pop-upsThey are shown on a TV for the whole room. Pop-up apps are meant for a home network and do not log in, so only add apps you trust. The push key must never be hard-coded in shared code.

▌Tasks app

The download includes Tasks, a big-screen to-do list written for anTV (Node.js 18 or newer, no installs). It is the reference app for pop-ups: tasks that are due trigger a card with Done, 10 min and Open buttons.

Set it up

  1. Windows, easiest: close anTV and run Setup-TVHub.bat -Tasks (installs Node.js and adds the card). Linux, from a terminal: close anTV and run python3 tvhub.py --add-node-app Tasks /path/to/tasks http://localhost:3000.

  2. By hand: Add app → A Node.js app…, project folder = the tasks folder, start command node server.js, address http://localhost:3000. Tick Show this app’s pop-ups and Keep its server running in the background.

  3. Check Settings → Pop-ups: it should say “1 of 1 connected”. In Tasks, open ⚙ Connect apps → 🔔 Send test pop-up to try it.

What Tasks does

  • Lists you can create, rename, recolor, duplicate and delete. Switch with the sidebar, LB/RB or ⏪ ⏩.
  • Due dates typed naturally (“milk tomorrow at 5pm”, “dentist dec 12 at 10:30”) or from a picker made for a remote. Overdue tasks turn red and sort first.
  • Voice (🎤): say a task with a date, “new list Groceries” or “switch to Chores”.
  • Quick add chips, Print, Archive, and Share as a view-only or editable link on your network.
  • Reminders: a pop-up with a chime 15 minutes before a task is due (change it with REMIND_LEAD_MIN).

Open it on this computer at http://localhost:3000 or from a phone or tablet using the “On your network” address it prints. Settings via environment: PORT, REMIND_LEAD_MIN, TASKS_DATA.

KeyboardFire TV remoteGamepad
MoveArrowsD-padD-pad / left stick
SelectEnterOKA
Back / closeEscBackB
VoiceVPlay/PauseX
Add taskNY
Prev / next list⏪ / ⏩LB / RB
List menuMenuStart
Quick addQSelect
Home network onlyTasks has no login. Anyone on your network who can reach it can open and change your lists.

▌Phone remote

Your phone becomes a remote through a small web page that anTV serves on your home Wi-Fi. It is off by default. No app to install.

Turn it on

  1. Open Settings → Remote & devices → Phone remote.

  2. Tick Enable phone remote. Keep the default port 8765 or change it. A 6-digit PIN is created for you (New PIN makes another).

  3. Save. On the home screen, the header now shows the address, the PIN and a QR code next to the clock.

Connect from your phone

  1. Join the same Wi-Fi as the PC. Scan the QR code, or type the address (for example http://192.168.1.50:8765) into the phone’s browser.

  2. Enter the PIN and tap Connect. The PIN is remembered in that browser. Five wrong guesses lock that device out for a minute.

The four tabs

The page fits one screen and never scrolls. The tab bar at the bottom switches panels, and your last tab is remembered.

Real render All four screens are the page from tvhub.py, rendered with the default app list. The top-right text shows “Home screen”, or “An app is running” while an app is open.

Touchpad gestures

GestureResult
Drag one fingerMove the cursor
TapLeft click
Two-finger tapRight click
Two-finger dragScroll
Press and hold, then dragDrag and drop
Hold buttonKeeps the left button down until you tap Release
SecurityTraffic is not encrypted. Use it only on a home network you trust. Anyone on the Wi-Fi who knows the PIN can control anTV. If you use a firewall (ufw), allow the port.
Linux extrasVolume uses pactl. The touchpad uses X11 (libXtst, or xdotool). Typing and keys for other apps need sudo apt install xdotool. Without them the phone shows an error for that action.

▌Fire TV remote & Xbox controller

Amazon Fire TV remote

  1. Hold the remote’s Home button for about 10 seconds until the LED blinks, then pair it in your system’s Bluetooth settings. It then behaves like a keyboard: D-pad = arrows, Select = Enter.

  2. Open Settings → Remote & devices → Remote control setup (Fire TV).

  3. Press any button to see its key name. Click Learn next to an action (Select, Back, Menu, Play/Pause, Home), then press the matching remote button. Reset restores the default.

  4. Teaching Home also creates a global “close app” hotkey on Linux. Buttons such as power, volume or app shortcuts may send nothing to a PC.

ActionEffect in anTV
SelectOpen the highlighted card
BackUp one folder (or close a dialog)
Menu (≡)Open Settings
Play/PauseOpen the highlighted card
HomeClose the running app and return to anTV

Xbox controller

  1. Wired: plug in by USB. Bluetooth (Linux): hold the pair button on top until the Xbox button flashes fast, then pair it in Mint’s Bluetooth settings. The Xbox wireless USB adapter needs the separate xone driver. Windows: uses the built-in XInput.

  2. Open Settings → Remote & devices → Game controller setup (Xbox) to see status and the last input seen, and to Learn any button.

DefaultAction
D-pad or left stickMove
ASelect
BBack
XPlay / Pause
StartMenu (settings; save and close inside the TV settings)
Xbox buttonClose the running app

Defaults follow the Linux xpad layout; other drivers number buttons differently, so use Learn if a button misbehaves.

▌Android apps

Install an APK

  1. Press I, or select + Install APK, or pick An Android APK… from the Add menu.

  2. Choose where to install: a device that adb can see, a new device by IP address, or Waydroid on this PC.

  3. Choose the APK (anTV looks in places like Downloads and USB drives). anTV installs it and offers to add a card that launches it.

Fire TV / Android TV setupTurn on ADB debugging in Developer options and allow apps from unknown sources, then connect by IP (an emulator is usually at 127.0.0.1:5555). For an Android phone, turn on USB debugging and plug it in.

Run Android on this PC (Waydroid)

  • anTV runs a nested weston compositor and places it on the TV screen with wmctrl, then starts the app with Waydroid. Closing the app stops the Waydroid session.
  • Check your setup first: Settings → Screen & browser → Android (Waydroid) check.
  • With an NVIDIA card, anTV uses software rendering automatically. Override it with “Android display”.

SmartTube

Choose Popular apps → SmartTube. It is not in any app store: download the APK only from the author’s official GitHub releases page (not APK mirror sites), put it in Downloads or on a USB stick, and anTV installs it into Waydroid and adds a card.

▌Local media & USB

  • Local Media opens a browser over your media folders. Choose files to play (anTV uses a media player such as VLC). Add or remove folders in Settings → Screen & browser.
  • USB drives get their own card when plugged in (detected through GIO on Linux, polled on Windows, where only removable drives are listed). Select the card to browse it.
  • Press E on a highlighted drive card to eject it safely.

▌Backup & your data

Settings → Your data (a tab in the classic dialog) has three actions.

ActionWhat it does
Save a backup of my data and settingsWrites one zip with config.json, your card images/, your backgrounds/ and a small info file. Browser logins (profiles) are not included.
Restore from a backupPick a backup zip. A zip without config.json is refused, unsafe paths are ignored, and picture paths from another computer are rewritten to this one. Both settings screens close afterwards.
Delete all data and start newAsks twice. Warning 1 offers “Save a backup first”; warning 2 defaults to No. It then removes the config, images, backgrounds, browser profiles and logs, restores the default cards and re-adds the default backgrounds.
Moving to a new PCSave a backup, copy the zip across, install anTV there, then use Restore from a backup. Sign in to your streaming sites again, because logins are not backed up.

▌Config & files

Settings are stored as JSON and can be edited by hand while anTV is closed.

PlatformFolder
Linux~/.config/tvhub/
Windows%APPDATA%\tvhub
  • config.json: your apps and options.
  • profiles/: one browser profile per service. images/: copies of chosen pictures. backgrounds/: the default backgrounds. logs/.
  • current.json: the running app. current.json.killed: a marker for deliberate stops.
Example app entries 
{ "name": "Netflix",  "type": "web",    "url": "https://www.netflix.com", "color": "#e50914", "favorite": true },

▌Limits & honesty

  • The launcher itself is ad-free. anTV does not and will not strip ads from Netflix, Hulu or Peacock. Their ad-free tiers need a subscription, and the content is DRM-protected.
  • SmartTube is a third-party app of the user’s own choosing. Take its APK only from the author’s official GitHub releases.
  • Tested: verified on Windows 11 and Linux Mint up to the features that existed then. Pop-ups, backup and default backgrounds are documented from the source.
  • Pop-ups: apps on Android or Fire TV cannot be listened to (use push from a bridge). Cards have no icons or pictures, and there is no per-app mute, quiet hours or history of missed pop-ups. Fire TV remote keys go to the running app, not to the pop-up (use the controller, the phone remote or the mouse). Rounded corners need a compositor, otherwise the card is square.
  • Android apps are practical on Linux only.
  • On Windows, a learned Fire TV “Home” key cannot become a global hotkey.
  • The Add/Edit form and file pickers are still normal dialogs (dark and large, but not full-screen overlays). Built-in cards cannot have pictures or be dragged. Open folders reset after Settings closes.

▌Troubleshooting

anTV opens on the wrong screen

Press F1 until it lands on the TV, or choose “Show anTV on” in Settings → Screen & browser.

I can’t get out of an app

Press Ctrl+Alt+K, or run python3 tvhub.py --kill from another terminal, or use the phone remote’s Close app / Home. On Linux, run python3 tvhub.py --install once so the global hotkeys exist.

The phone page won’t load

Check the phone is on the same Wi-Fi, that the address on the TV badge is the one you typed, and that the firewall allows the port (Windows installer switch -Firewall; Linux ufw). If it says “Too many wrong PINs”, wait a minute.

Phone typing or touchpad does nothing

On Linux install xdotool (sudo apt install xdotool). The touchpad also works through libXtst.

A remote button does the wrong thing

Open Remote control setup (or Game controller setup), press the button to see its name, then use Learn to assign it. Reset restores the default.

Android apps look wrong or fail

Run Settings → Screen & browser → Android (Waydroid) check and follow its message. Try “Always software (safest)” in Android display.

“anTV needs Android’s adb tool”

Linux: sudo apt install adb. Windows: winget install Google.PlatformTools (the 0.25.1 setup script no longer installs adb).
